item.title: Zverev banishes US Open demons with victory over Shelton
item.description: Zverev added the New York title to his collection after winning the French Open trophy earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: Top seed Alexander Zverev banished bitter U.S. Open memories to beat American Ben Shelton 6-3 7-6(2) 5-7 6-2 in the final on Sunday, capturing the title six years after letting a golden opportunity slip through his fingers. The German squandered a two-set lead in the 2020 title match against Austrian Dominic Thiem but now armed with a champion's mentality following his breakthrough triumph at Roland Garros in June, he broke American hearts with a devastating display against Shelton. "I think God has seen how hard we worked, how much we suffered, how much pain we went through and I think 2026 is the outcome of all the years that happened before," Zverev said during the presentation ceremony. The home fans were desperate to see Shelton end a 23-year American men's Grand Slam drought but the eighth seed never found his top form in his first major final. "I know that today 99.9% of the people wanted Ben to win so I'm very sorry," said Zverev. "Even though I know that the crowd was against me, the crowd was always incredibly fair and we as players we appreciate it." Zverev was so focused on the job at hand, he did not even realise he had won the title when Shelton smacked a service return long. As the umpire announced 'Game, set and match Zverev', the German headed back to the baseline, ready to receive Shelton's serve. It took him a few seconds to register why the cheering fans were giving him a standing ovation -- as he belatedly cracked a smile and ran to the net to embrace Shelton. He was beaming again as he was handed a Grand Slam record $5.5 million winner's prize. ZVEREV GETS HOT START In a battle between two of tennis' most explosive players, it was Zverev who had all the early firepower, as Shelton's inexperience showed with a double fault on break point in the opening game. Shelton produced one of the points of the match in the sixth game, scrambling to reach a drop shot and prevailing in a tense exchange at the net. Encouraged by his team, the American mixed in serve-and-volley tactics in an attempt to shift the momentum, but the move proved ineffective and he handed Zverev the set with a double fault. The partisan crowd tried to get under Zverev's skin in the second set, cheering wildly after he produced a double fault in the ninth game. But the German refused to get distracted, surging to a 5-0 lead in the tiebreak as the fans desperately chanted "Let's go, Ben!" Zverev looked like he would roll to the finish line in the third set as he saved a break point in the sixth game with a lethal backhand winner. Shelton's frustration boiled over two games later when he slipped and crashed to the court, prompting the American to let out an expletive. But Shelton dug in his heels, subduing his opponent with a series of powerful groundstrokes from the baseline to break serve and force a fourth set. Shelton's resilience only delayed the inevitable as Zverev came through a 25-shot rally to secure an early break in the deciding set. He never let go of that advantage as he finally got the chance to hoist the U.S. Open trophy on his 11th appearance at the hardcourt major. "My successes are a gift, the failures are a gift, and being here playing in front of you guys is a gift," said Shelton, the first Black American man in 54 years to contest the New York final after Arthur Ashe. The victory marked another step in Zverev's efforts to move beyond a series of painful Grand Slam disappointments. The German's career has also been overshadowed by off-court allegations of [USN:L6N42F07A TEXT:"domestic violence"] , which he has repeatedly denied. "We went 30 years without winning a Slam title and now won two in the span of three months," he said.

item.title: 投機筋が円買い越しに転換、2月末以来初 前週の円高進行
item.description:
Atsuko Aoyama
[東京 １４日 ロイター] - 投機筋が前週、２月末以来で初めて円の買い越しに転換したこと...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
投機筋が円買い越し転換、2月末以来　円キャリー巻き戻し終了の見方 6:55 配信

日本円と米ドルの紙幣。2023年3月10日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Atsuko Aoyama

[東京 １４日 ロイター] - 投機筋が前週、２月末以来で初めて円の買い越しに転換したことが最新のデータ（８日時点）で分かった。市場では円のポジションが中立化され、円キャリーの巻き戻しがいったん終了したとの見方が聞かれる。８日にはドルが１５２円台まで下落し、１６０円超で推移していた月初から７円以上円高が進行していた。

米商品先物取引委員会（ＣＦＴＣ）が１４日までに公表した建玉報告によると、投機筋のポジション動向を映すとされるＩＭＭ通貨先物非商業部門の８日時点の取り組み状況で、円の買い越しは１万０７９６枚と、９万２２２７枚の売り越しだった前の週から買い越しに転換した。買い越しに転じたのは２月２４日時点のデータ以来初めて。

市場では「円キャリーの巻き戻しがいったん終了し、ポジションが中立化された。ドルが１５２円を下回る可能性がかなり減った」（あおぞら銀行の諸我晃チーフ・マーケット・ストラテジスト）との声が聞かれた。市場では前週の円高進行の背景として、日銀の利上げペース加速に関する思惑や日米当局による円安是正の意向が指摘されている。

データの内訳をみると、円の売り建玉は１６万７９９５枚と、前の週の２０万９３９６枚から２割弱減少。一方、円の買い建玉は１７万８７９１枚で、１１万７１６９枚から５割以上増加、２０２５年１２月初旬以来の多さとなった。

円売りと円買いの双方の建玉が残存していることを巡り、「双方に巻き戻しのリスクがある」（ＳＭＢＣ日興証券の丸山凜途シニア金利・為替ストラテジスト）との声も聞かれる。円売りの建玉は３月末の水準に減っているものの、２０２４年７月の介入後に約１５円の円高が生じた２０２４年８月中旬の６万３９９７枚を１０万枚以上上回っている。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：40年ぶり円安で介入警戒、「暗黒月曜」再現はあるか　変動マグマ蓄積 アングル：政府・日銀の為替介入余力、値踏みする市場　「神通力」どこまで アングル：介入後も残る円買い、ベセント期待が後押し　肩透かしなら円安リスク アングル：為替介入までの「距離」、市場で読み合い活発化　160円警戒とも アングル：ドル上昇の裏に円キャリーの思惑、ためらう投資家　継続性に疑問 最終更新: 9/14(月) 8:57 ロイター

item.title: Diamondbacks DFA former All-Star OF Lourdes Gurriel Jr.
item.description: The Arizona Diamondbacks designated outfielder Lourdes Gurriel Jr. for assignment Sunday, three years after the Cuban was one of the key players on their 2023 World Series team.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Arizona Diamondbacks designated outfielder Lourdes Gurriel Jr. for assignment Sunday, three years after the Cuban was one of the key players on their 2023 World Series team. Gurriel was batting just .210 with two home runs and 22 RBIs in 51 games during an injury-plagued season. He tore the ACL in his right knee last September and didn't make his season debut until April 18, and he later dealt with hamstring and adductor issues. In 2023, Gurriel was an All-Star when he belted a career-best 24 homers while batting .261 with 82 RBIs. In 17 postseason games, he batted .273 with three homers and 11 RBIs. Arizona lost to the Texas Rangers in the World Series. "It was a very difficult move," Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo told reporters Sunday. "The discussion with Lourdes last night was painful for all of us. He has meant so much to this organization, carried at times, led us to a World Series, has been a dependable bat, a great teammate, a big influence in that clubhouse, and to say goodbye to that is never easy." Gurriel was in the final season of a three-year, $42 million deal. The team held a $14 club option for 2027 but wasn't expected to exercise it. The buyout was $5 million. Gurriel, 32, was finishing up his fourth season with Arizona. He was acquired prior to the 2023 season after playing five campaigns for the Toronto Blue Jays. Overall, Gurriel has a .271 average with 131 homers and 513 RBIs in 926 career games. The Diamondbacks are trying to chase down the San Diego Padres for the final National League wild-card berth. The urgency meant the club could no longer be patient for Gurriel to break out of his funk. "The at-bats, at times, lacked a little bit of consistency," Lovullo said. "With where we are at this point in the season, we didn't have the time to get him to that place where he could be that Lourdes Gurriel we remember." Arizona recalled infielder Jose Fernandez from Triple-A Reno in a corresponding move. Fernandez, who turns 23 on Sept. 22, batted .262 with three homers and 16 RBIs in 65 games with the Diamondbacks earlier this season. Arizona also demoted veteran Zac Gallen to the bullpen and fellow right-hander Michael Soroka will start in his spot on Tuesday against the Miami Marlins. Gallen, 31, will pitch in long relief. The 2023 All-Star is just 3-9 with a 6.22 ERA in 20 starts this season. Gallen has started 196 games -- 189 for Arizona, seven for the Miami Marlins -- without pitching in relief over his eight big-league seasons. "I just feel like Mike, at this time, is going to give us the best chance to win a baseball game," Lovullo said of the move. --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina out vs. UNC, Tait Reynolds to start
item.description: The Clemson Tigers will turn to freshman Tait Reynolds at quarterback against North Carolina on Saturday with Christopher Vizzina expected to miss the game due to an elbow injury, according to multiple reports.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Clemson Tigers will turn to freshman Tait Reynolds at quarterback against North Carolina on Saturday with Christopher Vizzina expected to miss the game due to an elbow injury, according to multiple reports. Vizzina left Saturday's 22-7 win over Georgia Southern with an injury to his non-throwing elbow that is expected to sideline him for 1-2 weeks. He was 4-for-7 with 19 yards passing, a touchdown and an interception when he left the game. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said at halftime that Vizzina was going to go back in the game but "couldn't feel his left arm." Reynolds, who also saw time in Clemson's 51-10 season-opening loss to LSU, was 16 of 27 passing for 178 yards against Georgia Southern. The freshman from Queen Creek, Ariz., is still seeking his first career touchdown pass but has completed 60.6% of his pass attempts through two games. Clemson (1-1) plays host to North Carolina before traveling to play at California on Sept. 25. --Field Level Media

item.title: Sassuolo beat Juventus 3-2 after late drama, Napoli return to winning ways
item.description: Juventus suffered a 3-2 defeat following a frantic finish at Sassuolo on Sunday, while Napoli snapped a three-match losing run with a 1-0 home win over Bologna as both sides continued their inconsistent starts to the Serie A season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Juventus suffered a 3-2 defeat following a frantic finish at Sassuolo on Sunday, while Napoli snapped a three-match losing run with a 1-0 home win over Bologna as both sides continued their inconsistent starts to the Serie A season. Juventus have started the season in disappointing fashion, picking up seven points from four matches to sit eighth in the table, while Napoli are 10th with six points. After a largely uneventful first hour, Sassuolo broke the deadlock in the 65th minute when Nemanja Matic slipped a precise pass into the area for Sebastiano Esposito, who finished with a slick one-touch stroke. Juventus levelled in the 82nd minute after Sassuolo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric misjudged a cross, allowing Edon Zhegrova to tap into an empty net. The hosts thought they had sealed victory in the 89th minute when Darryl Bakola teed up Kieron Bowie, who curled a first-time effort into the corner. Zhegrova looked to have rescued a point for Juventus when he fired home from the edge of the area in stoppage time to complete his brace, but Sassuolo had the final say. Four minutes into stoppage time, Vasilije Adzic controlled a deep cross and curled in a superb finish into the far corner to seal victory for Sassuolo with virtually the last kick of the game. NAPOLI BREAK LOSING STREAK Napoli ended their recent slump as Stanislav Lobotka turned in a second-half winner to secure all three points at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. Massimiliano Allegri's side entered the clash under pressure following consecutive league defeats to Como and Inter Milan, as well as a midweek Champions League loss to Arsenal. Napoli dominated possession early on, but Bologna thought they had taken the lead in the seventh minute when Arthur Theate headed home. The effort was ruled out for offside following a VAR review. Lobotka eventually broke the deadlock in the 66th minute, scoring the game's only goal to hand Napoli all three points. Napoli secured the points despite an ongoing injury crisis, with key figures Scott McTominay, Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa, and goalkeeper Alex Meret among those sidelined. Further concern arose late in the match when midfielder Kevin De Bruyne was forced off, though Allegri quickly played down fears of a serious setback. "He expended a lot of energy, it was cramp," Allegri told reporters. "Today the game was wanted and won with anger, something that was missing in recent matches. There we were too superficial, even though we did some good things."

item.title: North Korea held live-fire drills involving artillery and missiles, KCNA says
item.description: North Korea held a live-fire drill to test long-range artillery and missile units of its army, state media KCNA reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea held a live-fire drill to test long-range artillery and missile units of its army, state media KCNA reported on Monday. The "joint firepower attack drill" on Saturday involved five army units and tested several weapon systems, including various attack drones, tactical cruise missiles, tactical ballistic missiles, and large-caliber multiple rocket launchers, KCNA said. The drill would boost the morale of the troops and improve their capabilities to "completely collapse the enemy" anytime an order is placed, KCNA said citing an artillery director. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff [USN:L1N4530VM TEXT:"said"] on Saturday that North Korea fired several short-range ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast, followed by a joint military exercise among South Korea, Japan and the United States.

item.title: Giants 1B Rafael Devers (core) to undergo season-ending surgery
item.description: The San Francisco Giants placed star first baseman Rafael Devers on the 60-day injured list with an injured core muscle on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The San Francisco Giants placed star first baseman Rafael Devers on the 60-day injured list with an injured core muscle on Sunday. The move ends Devers' season, with surgery for the injury likely to occur in the coming days. He'll be meeting with doctors for a consultation on Monday. Outfielder Scott Bandura will be Devers' roster replacement, moving up from Triple-A Sacramento. The Giants said in a release that Devers "has managed this issue for much of the season and chose to keep playing through it." The 29-year-old Devers is a three-time All-Star and a two-time Silver Slugger who helped the Boston Red Sox win the 2018 World Series. Despite the injury, Devers has knocked in 98 RBIs, slammed 37 home runs and hit an MLB-leading 36 doubles on a .258 batting average this season. The 37 home runs are the second-highest total of his career. Devers, who has batted as the designated hitter in recent games, has 100 appearances at first base this season and 48 at DH. Bandura, 25, is a former seventh-round draft pick who will be making his major league debut. He batted .320 with 13 homers and 94 RBIs during stops with Triple-A Sacramento and Double-A Richmond this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: UK PM Burnham to meet business leaders to discuss growth
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will meet the bosses of several major companies on Monday to discuss his plans to generate economic growth, his office said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will meet the bosses of several major companies on Monday to discuss his plans to generate economic growth, his office said. Burnham will host a reception with the chief executives of companies including banks HSBC (HSBA.L) and Standard Chartered (STAN.L) , oil majors BP (BP.L) and Shell (SHEL.L) , and telecom firms BT (BT.L) and Vodafone (VOD.L) . He will say his plans for devolution can help deliver much-needed infrastructure and will look to support a culture shift to back innovation. The meeting with the bosses of Britain's biggest energy companies follows a report Burnham is set [USN:L8N4530WC TEXT:"to delay a decision"] on whether to bring the Shell-backed Jackdaw gas field online until after a parliamentary by-election next month. Ahead of the reception, he will hold a roundtable with British entrepreneurs from the fields of fintech, AI, clean energy and advanced manufacturing. Burnham's finance minister John Healey last week used [USN:L1N44Z06Z TEXT:"his first major speech"] since taking office to set out a brighter vision for the economy before an annual budget where he faces tough tax and spending choices.

item.title: Vikings QB Kyler Murray (concussion) ruled out vs. Packers
item.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was ruled out of Sunday's game against the visiting Green Bay Packers after suffering a concussion on scramble in the first quarter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was ruled out of Sunday's game against the visiting Green Bay Packers after suffering a concussion on scramble in the first quarter. Murray took a hard hit to the side of his head and had his helmet knocked off as he slid short of the first-down marker with 6:10 to go in the opening quarter. He stayed on the turf while medical staff attended to him. Eventually, Murray got to his feet and walked to the locker room without assistance. The team announced in the second quarter that Murray had been ruled out for the remainder of the game. Packers safety Javon Bullard was penalized 15 yards for unnecessary roughness on the play. Carson Wentz replaced Murray at quarterback. The Vikings made headlines earlier this month when they named the veteran Wentz as their No. 2 quarterback ahead of former first-round pick JJ McCarthy. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brandon Lowe's pinch-hit heroics help Pirates evade sweep by Cubs
item.description: Brandon Lowe drove in two runs with a pinch-hit single in the sixth inning as the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Chicago Cubs 4-3 Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brandon Lowe drove in two runs with a pinch-hit single in the sixth inning as the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Chicago Cubs 4-3 Sunday. The Cubs (83-67) fell into a tie with the Phillies for the first National League wild-card spot. Philadelphia beat Atlanta 9-4 Sunday. Chicago hosts the Braves in a three-game series starting Monday. The Pirates (75-75) avoided the sweep with the win. Cubs starter Matthew Boyd (8-5) gave up seven hits and four runs in 5 1/3 innings. The southpaw walked two and struck out three in 88 pitches. Pirates starter Bubba Chandler (8-9) gave up five hits and three runs in 5 1/3 innings. The right-hander walked four and struck out three in 90 pitches. Mason Montgomery picked up his 13th save with a scoreless ninth inning. The Pirates started the scoring in the first when Konnor Griffin led off with a single and Oneil Cruz walked. Bryan Reynolds singled in Griffin for a 1-0 lead. Chandler only allowed one Cub to reach second base through 4 2/3 innings before Chicago broke through. Pedro Ramirez started the rally with a two-out walk, setting up Miguel Amaya for a two-run home run to left to put the Cubs in front 2-1. The Pirates fought back in the sixth when Reynolds walked to lead off and Rafael Flores Jr. singled. Nick Gonzales followed with a long drive to right over the head of Seiya Suzuki. The ball was lost in the ivy for a ground-rule double that tied the game 2-2. Boyd struck out Ryan O'Hearn for the first out of the inning, and Aaron Civale replaced him to face Jake Mangum. Mangum walked and Lowe followed with his single to center, scoring Flores and Gonzales to make it 4-2 Pirates. The Cubs cut it to one in the sixth when Michael Busch singled with one out and Alex Bregman doubled to left. Ian Happ walked to load the bases and Busch scored when Nico Hoerner grounded out. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alec Burlseon gives Cards win over White Sox with one swing
item.description: Alec Burleson hit a go-ahead, bases-clearing double in the bottom of the sixth inning and Michael McGreevy pitched six effective innings Sunday afternoon for the host St. Louis Cardinals in a 3-1 victory over the Chicago White Sox.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alec Burleson hit a go-ahead, bases-clearing double in the bottom of the sixth inning and Michael McGreevy pitched six effective innings Sunday afternoon for the host St. Louis Cardinals in a 3-1 victory over the Chicago White Sox. Chicago put its first two runners aboard in the ninth and loaded the bases with two outs, but Colson Montgomery flied to medium center field against George Soriano. Montgomery also made a key error earlier that set up Burleson's big hit. Reaching the postseason remains unlikely for the Cardinals (74-76), but they made a definite impact on the American League Central race after taking two of three from the first-place White Sox. A day after mounting a ninth-inning comeback to stop a four-game losing streak and increase their division lead, the White Sox (76-73) saw the Cleveland Guardians creep within a half-game of first place after beating the Minnesota Twins on Sunday. The White Sox, who have dropped 10 of 14, head to Cleveland for a three-game showdown starting Monday night. White Sox rookie right-hander David Sandlin retired his first 16 batters before Nathan Church blooped a single to right with one out in the bottom of the sixth. The No. 9 hitter, Masyn Winn, followed with another bloop single to left, which brought White Sox pitching coach Zach Bove to the mound for a meeting. Sandlin responded by striking out Bryan Torres for the second out, but Ivan Herrera reached to load the bases when Montgomery booted a routine-looking grounder to short. White Sox manager Will Venable called on left-hander Chris Murphy to face Burleson. Burleson, a lefty who is much weaker against same-sided pitchers, did a great job fighting off a pitch on his hands, dumping a three-run double inside the line in right. It gave him 109 RBIs, putting him in the major league lead at the time. Sandlin (2-2) allowed three unearned runs and two hits to go with five strikeouts over 5 2/3 innings. He's in his third stint this season with the White Sox, having been recalled from Triple-A after Saturday's comeback win. The White Sox continued to struggle with runners in scoring position, going 0-for-7 and stranding seven overall. They failed to add any runs after Sam Antonacci led off the sixth with a triple. McGreevy (7-9) allowed a run, three hits and three walks with six strikeouts after posting a 6.26 ERA over his previous nine starts. Gordon Graceffo struck out three in two scoreless innings, and Soriano converted his fourth save despite the traffic. The Cardinals came in 7 1/2 games back in the NL Wild Card chase. --Field Level Media

item.title: Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc seen winning by one seat, election authority projects
item.description: Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc is projected to win a one-seat majority in Sunday's vote for parliament, the election authority said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc is projected to win a one-seat majority in Sunday's vote for parliament, the election authority said. The bloc, headed by Social Democrats party leader Magdalena Andersson, was expected to win 175 seats in the 349-seat parliament, the agency projected based on votes from 4,853 of Sweden's 6,312 election districts. The right-wing governing bloc was seen winning 174 seats.

item.title: Trump says US could stay in Iran and keep oil, like Venezuela deal
item.description: Trump reiterated that he expected the Iran war to end this year, possibly just after the US midterm elections in November.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

World

Trump says US could stay in Iran and keep oil, like Venezuela deal

Trump reiterated that he expected the Iran war to end this year, possibly just after the US midterm elections in November.

US President Trump, center, walks from Marine One to board Air Force One, Aug. 21, 2026, at Joint Base Andrews, MD, en route to South Carolina. (Photo: AP/Jacquelyn Martin)

DOONBEG, Ireland: US President Donald Trump suggested on Sunday (Sep 13) that the US could stay in Iran and "keep the oil", drawing a parallel with a US push to take control of a fifth of Venezuela's vast oil reserves. On a trip to Ireland for meetings and to watch golf, he reiterated that he still expected the Iran war to end this year, possibly just after midterm elections due in the US in November. Speaking at the Irish Open golf championship, Trump added that the price of petrol would "drop like a rock" once the Iran war ended. Turmoil in the Middle East has roiled oil markets, with oil traders expecting prices to rise again on Monday after an attack on a Saudi oil pipeline. Trump said he would only make the "right deal" and would not do one that was "no good", adding that Iran was "calling constantly" for peace talks, an assertion that Tehran has dismissed in the past. But the president also introduced another option: staying engaged with Iran. He drew a parallel with the US deal in Venezuela, announced in August. "We'll ultimately get out (of Iran), unless we decide to stay and keep the oil like Venezuela," Trump said, adding that US revenue from Venezuela has "paid for the war many times".
